name: ADM208EARSZ-REEL
title: ADM206E/ADM207E/ADM208E/ADM211E/ADM213E ±15 kV ESD-protected 5 V RS-232 drivers and receivers
summary: A family of RS-232 / V.28 transceivers that run from one 5 V supply, making their own ±9 V rails with an on-chip charge pump and four 0.1 µF capacitors. The ADM208E has four drivers and four receivers; its siblings trade driver and receiver counts and add shutdown and receiver-enable pins. Every RS-232 pin withstands ±15 kV air and ±8 kV contact discharge, and data runs at up to 230 kbps.
key_figures: 3.5 mA typ, 13 mA max, no load
±9.0 V typ, ±5.0 V min into 3 kΩ
±15 kV HBM and air, ±8 kV contact

circuits.title: ADM208E typical operating circuit
circuits.description: The ADM208E on a single 5 V supply with its five 0.1 µF capacitors: C1 across C1+/C1- feeds the doubler, C2 across C2+/C2- feeds the inverter, C3 holds V+ against VCC, C4 holds V- against ground and C5 bypasses VCC to ground. 4 logic inputs drive 4 RS-232 outputs and 4 RS-232 inputs return to 4 logic outputs.
notes: Each logic input has a 400 kΩ pull-up and each RS-232 input a 5 kΩ pull-down inside the chip.

operation.text: Five RS-232 / V.28 line driver and receiver chips that run from one 5 V rail and need four external 0.1 µF capacitors for the charge pump. They differ in driver and receiver count and in whether they have shutdown and receiver-enable pins (selection table). All meet EIA-232E and CCITT V.28 and run up to 230 kbps. They are drop-in upgrades for MAX2xxE parts and for the older ADM2xx and AD230 to AD241 families.
ADM207E and ADM208E come in 24-lead PDIP, SOIC, SSOP and TSSOP; ADM206E in 24-lead SOIC only; ADM211E and ADM213E in 28-lead SOIC, SSOP and TSSOP. A Z in the part number marks a Pb-free part;

A 200 kHz oscillator drives a switch matrix that first doubles 5 V to about +10 V using C1, then inverts that to about -10 V using C2. C3 and C4 smooth the ripple on V+ and V-. Any of C1 to C4 may be raised up to 47 µF, easing direct substitution for older charge-pump RS-232 transceivers. V+ and V- can feed a small external load; they fall from about +10 V and -9 V unloaded to about +8.2 V and -4.2 V at 18 mA.

Each driver turns a 5 V logic level into an inverted EIA-232 level, typically ±9 V into an EIA-232 load at VCC = 5 V. An open driver input is pulled high by its 400 kΩ resistor, which holds that output low. A grounded input draws about 8 µA through the pull-up, so to save power an unused input is left open or tied to VCC.

Each receiver is an inverting level shifter from EIA-232 to 5 V logic with a Schmitt input of 0.65 V hysteresis, which copes with noise and slow edges. The 5 kΩ pull-down holds an open input at 0 V, so an open or grounded input gives a logic 1 at the output. The inputs withstand ±25 V; the switching thresholds are guaranteed between 0.4 V and 2.4 V.

The enable pin puts the receiver outputs in high impedance so several can share a bus. Shutdown stops the charge pump and the drivers; on the ADM211E every receiver output goes high impedance, while on the ADM213E receivers R4 and R5 stay active so a peripheral can wake the host. Driver outputs are switched off in shutdown but are not high impedance, so driver outputs must not be tied together. Power in shutdown falls to between 1 µW and 5 µW. Shutdown is asserted by a high level on the ADM211E and by a low level on the ADM213E. The charge pump needs about 100 µs after leaving shutdown to settle.

The enable input is driven between 0 V and 3 V. tER runs from the enable edge until the receiver output crosses +3.5 V (rising) or +0.8 V (falling); tDR runs from the disable edge until the output has moved 0.1 V away from VOH or VOL. For the ADM213E the enable sense is inverted.
With worst-case loading the outputs keep valid RS-232 levels at 230 kb/s. The output slew rate is held inside the chip below 30 V/µs to limit EMI.

Every RS-232 input and output carries two back-to-back clamp diodes made as large p-n junctions. At normal RS-232 levels one of them is always reverse biased; above about ±50 V they break down and clamp, carrying surge currents of several amperes. Receiver inputs also shed energy through their 5 kΩ resistor to GND. The structure gives ±15 kV ESD and ±2 kV EFT protection on all RS-232 lines.

All pins are tested against all other pins to MIL-STD-883B, and every I-O pin to IEC1000-4-2, with the part powered and running, powered and shut down, and unpowered. The I-O pins meet IEC1000-4-2 level 4: over 8 kV contact and over 15 kV air discharge.
Tested with unshielded cables under worst-case conditions, the parts meet classification 2: data is corrupted during the burst and resumes on its own as soon as it ends.
The parts meet classification 1 (normal operation) at level 3, 10 V/m. Fields up to 30 V/m caused no degradation and data kept flowing without errors during exposure.

The charge-pump switches are break-before-make, so no current spike runs from VCC to GND during switching, and conducted emissions stay well under the EN55022 / CISPR22 limits with nothing more than the 0.1 µF capacitor.

Controlled output slew keeps radiated emissions low while still supporting 230 kBaud. Measured in a shielded anechoic chamber with the parts at maximum baud rate in a typical RS-232 link, emissions stay inside the limits with no added shielding or filtering.
